articles.title_orig: Column | I went to Mexico to test-drive the cars Americans can’t buy
articles.title_zh: Column | I went to Mexico to test-drive the cars Americans can’t buy
articles.content_orig:
The unstoppable advance of Chinese automakers into the Mexican market—which continues to see record sales volumes —has dispelled all doubt: they’re here to stay, and it’s only a matter of time before they begin assembling vehicles in the country.
Their motivation lies not only in consolidating their presence in Mexico and the rest of Latin America, but also in meeting, as much as possible, the requirements necessary to export their products to the United States in the event that the market eventually opens up to these brands.
One of the automakers with a global presence that is already acting in anticipation of the inevitable is Nissan, the sales leader in Mexico by volume, whose executives estimate that its Chinese competitors will begin manufacturing cars here within three years, while their entry into the U.S. market will eventually occur, though “not before five years.”
This warning was recently issued by Christian Meunier, the executive in charge of Nissan’s operations throughout the Americas, during a conference in Tokyo where he explained that the consolidation of Chinese brands in Mexico “will trigger fierce price competition that will force Nissan and other traditional manufacturers to cut costs immediately or risk losing market share,” according to a report by AutoNews .
Meunier added that the Japanese automaker has already begun restructuring its costs and product development to prepare for this new wave of rivals.
“We have a very ambitious plan in Mexico, especially to reduce costs and be able to compete with Chinese manufacturers when they localize their production—which will likely happen in the next two or three years—so we must be prepared,” he emphasized.
One of the first measures implemented by Nissan was the introduction to the Mexican market of a hybrid pickup produced by its partner, Zhengzhou Nissan Automobile Co.
The Chinese Onslaught in Numbers
With this decision, the Tokyo-based automaker joins an ever-growing group of automotive companies—such as Ford, General Motors (GM), and Stellantis—that are leveraging production capacity through joint ventures in China to compete in the local market with models imported from that region.
This trend has led to a situation where, by the third quarter of this year, nearly 30% of the vehicles sold in the Mexican automotive market originated from a Chinese assembly plant, regardless of whether they bear the emblem of a Chinese brand or that of a U.S. or European company.
Official figures from INEGI indicate that as of the end of September, China-based brands delivered 130,488 units in the country. However, it is worth noting that this data excludes at least four competitors that do not report their monthly results to the government agency, including BYD, the Chinese automaker that leads in sales in the domestic market according to unofficial estimates.
Experts estimate that total deliveries by Chinese-origin brands in Mexico amounted to 206,679 vehicles in the first nine months of the year. However, to this volume must be added the sales of models imported from China by other global brands—a figure that exceeds 149,000 units, according to INEGI.
This results in a total of nearly 356,000 Chinese-made vehicles sold in the country, while actual sales volume for the period in question would amount to just over 1,220,000 vehicles. Based on these estimates, the market share of vehicles manufactured in China—regardless of brand—stands at 29.2% of the total.
Nissan and the other global brands will be joined by Volkswagen, which confirmed in late September that the first units of the Lamando L sedan destined for the Mexican market have already rolled off the assembly line at its partner SAIC Volkswagen and are on their way, with plans to be displayed at dealerships across the country before the end of the year.

articles.title_orig: There’s not enough money in the world to pay for the AI boom
articles.title_zh: There’s not enough money in the world to pay for the AI boom
articles.content_orig:
Get an introductory Jacobin subscription for just $20
F or an industry that we’re told is central to our collective future, the artificial intelligence (AI) industry increasingly seems to be built on a combination of artificially inflated hopes and bad accounting.
The industry’s critics have been raising concerns about its finances for a while: the fact that most of its flagship firms are grossly unprofitable , that they’ve had to jack up their prices to try break even (leading their business customers to pump the brakes on using their products), or that many of the eye-popping investment announcements that are meant to show demand for AI is strong have actually been circular financing — meaning different AI firms cycling money to and from each other.
But none of it has seemed to slow the industry’s boom or the relentless hype machine behind it. Until now, anyway. It used to be that you mostly heard concerns about the industry’s underlying economics in newspapers, blogs, social media posts, and podcasts, and that those concerns went completely unreflected in the markets. But these concerns seem now to have finally bled over into investors’ thinking.

articles.title_orig: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite
articles.title_zh: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27.2 launched this week with many new features for iPhone users, including a Messages addition that was previously announced for iOS 27 but later got pushed back: Suggestions.
Throughout the iOS 27 beta this summer, one of my favorite AI features was a Messages addition that didn’t feel like AI at all: Suggestions.
Here’s what they do, per Apple :
Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.
Suggestions appear as small, convenient action buttons beneath messages they’re relevant to.
As seen in the image below, if someone asks you to do something, you might see a suggestion to add to Reminders or Notes. Or if an event is mentioned, suggestions lets you easily add it to your calendar.
Suggestions worked well for me in the iOS 27 beta, but shortly before the public launch last month, Apple delayed the feature into a “future software update.”
Now in iOS 27.2, suggestions have officially returned, launching for all users. And one way they’ve changed might explain why they were pulled in the first place.
As I mentioned, suggestions performed as expected for me during the summer. But if I had one complaint, it was that they sometimes appeared when a message’s context didn’t merit them. At times I saw suggestions to add things to Notes, Reminders, or Calendar when there wasn’t a clear justification for these recommendations.
But in iOS 27.2, I’ve seen far fewer suggestions appearing in my Messages conversations. When I see them, it’s always obvious why they’re being offered. Clearly the feature benefited from a little extra fine tuning.
If you want even more control over the types of Suggestions that appear, you can manually configure categories under Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Messages ⇾ Suggested Actions.
How have suggestions been working for you in iOS 27.2? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title_orig: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
articles.title_zh: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
articles.content_orig:
United Parcel Service on Tuesday reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The guidance raise comes after the company already upped its outlook last quarter . UPS now said it's projecting full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion.
Shares of UPS rose slightly in morning trading.
Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Sept. 30, UPS reported net income of $1.16 billion, or $1.37 per share, down slightly from net income of $1.31 billion, or $1.55, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time expenses, UPS reported earnings per share of $1.69. Revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion.
In its domestic segment, the company said it saw a 4.5% increase in revenue, while its international segment had a 7.1% rise in revenue. Its supply chain solutions business saw an 18.2% revenue increase, which UPS said was primarily driven to growth in forwarding and logistics, including healthcare . On a call with analysts, CEO Carol Tomé said healthcare revenue exceeded $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter.
The company had previously said it expected its third-quarter domestic revenue to be flat and for domestic average daily volume to fall due to seasonal declines and the glide down with Amazon .
"We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network," Tomé said on the call. "All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."
UPS has been in the midst of a turnaround under Tomé's leadership, working to create a leaner business model and leveraging automation to position the company for growth.
As the company prepares for its peak holiday season, Tomé said the consumer remains resilient, and the growth in average daily volume between the third and fourth quarters will be consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume is expected to fall due to the reduction with Amazon.
She added that nearly 70% of all packages will flow through an automated process this holiday season.

articles.title_orig: Honda warns 50% Canada auto tariffs would be catastrophic for auto industry
articles.title_zh: Honda warns 50% Canada auto tariffs would be catastrophic for auto industry
articles.content_orig:
DETROIT — The automotive industry faces a "catastrophic" scenario if the U.S. and Canada cannot reach a new trade deal by the end of this year, an executive with Honda Motor warned Tuesday.
President Donald Trump has threatened to double tariffs on Canadian vehicles and parts from 25% to 50% on Jan. 1 if the two countries don't reach a deal.
"That really would be catastrophic for the entire industry," Jennifer Thomas, senior vice president of corporate affairs at American Honda Motor Co., said during a Reuters automotive conference in Detroit.
Thomas said, ideally, the countries would also include Mexico in the arrangement and reach a trilateral deal, like the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, or USMCA. Trade associations representing Honda, as well as every major player in the U.S. automotive industry, have been advocating for that more comprehensive accord and against bilateral arrangements between two countries.
Her comments come months after U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced that the U.S. would not automatically extend the USMCA, moving the trade pact into an annual review process instead of a 16-year trilateral extension.
Trump negotiated the USMCA to replace the North American Free Trade Agreement during his first term and it took effect in 2020. He later soured on it and accused Canada of "ripping off the United States of America for years."
Thomas said she is "cautiously optimistic" that cooler heads will prevail to avoid the doubling of tariffs, which Trump threatened in August if no deal can be reached.
She said she's encouraged by recent reports that the U.S. and Canada have reestablished trade talks, including easing levies on critical materials such as aluminum.
"Our message has been clear: We need that trilateral agreement to stay in place in order for the U.S. industry to be competitive," Thomas said. "It's integral to our success."
Honda is the s econd-largest producer of vehicles in Canada behind Toyota Motor , but many automotive officials have voiced concerns about the lack of a North American trade deal and tariff uncertainty due to the number of parts that regularly cross the borders for vehicle production.
While Honda has established large operations in Canada, the company reports that more than 60% of the vehicles it sells in the U.S. are manufactured domestically across multiple U.S. assembly plants.
"I never thought I would see the North American region be put at a disadvantage like this," Thomas said, adding that some overseas countries have better tariff rates.
The Trump administration has negotiated trade deals with other countries such as Japan and South Korea, which are major exporters of vehicles to the U.S., that include 15% tariffs on vehicles.

articles.title_orig: Two men charged in UK over RAF Fairford incident allegedly linked to Iran
articles.title_zh: Two men charged in UK over RAF Fairford incident allegedly linked to Iran
articles.content_orig:
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, (left) and Nouman Essghir, 24, attended court on Tuesday
Two British nationals have appeared in court in connection to an alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford in September.
Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, from Westminster, London, has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police earlier said they believed to be Iran.
Nouman Essghir, also 24 and from Westminster, has been charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on 22 August - weeks before he was arrested near the airbase in Gloucestershire alongside four other men.
The pair appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.
A major incident was declared after three suspicious vans were seen near the US-operated airbase on 27 September.
Dozens of residents were evacuated and a large cordon was put up in the area around the base. No explosive materials were found in the vans by police but a quantity of petrol was seized.
The court heard vans bearing the logo "Fuel2You" were spotted close to the base.
In the early hours, the vans came across a Ministry of Defence Police cordon and re-routed to another location.
Police arrived and arrested five men. They later revealed that one had called 999 and reported what was going on.
During the hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court, Essghir stood in the dock wearing a grey sweatshirt and confirmed his name and address.
Abdulkarim is charged with helping with the plot.
He appeared in court in a wheelchair wearing a checked shirt, jeans and a baseball cap. He confirmed his name and address.
Both men are charged under the 2023 National Security Act.
They were told the case will be next heard at the Old Bailey on 20 November.
Mohmed Abdulkarim seen leaving Westminster Magistrates' Court
Essghir was one of five men arrested near the base on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act and later on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act. All five were released on police bail the following day, but Essghir was re-arrested on 20 October.
A 25-year-old UK-Iranian national who was also re-arrested on that date on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service has now been released without charge. He remains on police bail after his initial arrest on 1 October on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts.
The re-arrests in October led to detectives interviewing Abdulkarim.
Eight men have been arrested as part of the counter-terror police investigation.
Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor said the release of the five men on police bail in September had raised significant questions and speculation about the investigation for members of the public.
He stressed that tactics used by counter-terror police can appear "illogical" at times but said that "there will always be a good reason or rationale behind them".
"In this case, this decision-making has led to swifter progress, better evidence, and ultimately us securing the charges that I've announced today," he added.
Watch: 'A range of incidents' believed to have been directed by Iran in recent months
US President Donald Trump at the time said he was "surprised" the men had been released, saying: "We would not have released them."
Taylor said counter-terror police had seen "a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state".
Iran has previously denied any involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford.
The base has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.
In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base to the Middle East, after the UK approved a request for it to be used for defensive strikes against Iran.
After the incident in September the US pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America.
Trump said the aircraft were removed due to "some threats" to the base, without giving specific details.

articles.title_orig: Russia committed war crimes in Ukraine by attacking its energy grid, UN-backed inquiry says
articles.title_zh: Russia committed war crimes in Ukraine by attacking its energy grid, UN-backed inquiry says
articles.content_orig:
Russia is committing war crimes and crimes against humanity by intentionally attacking civilian infrastructure – including vital energy systems – in Ukraine, an independent UN investigations panel said on Monday.
Russian forces have been targeting Ukrainian power infrastructure since the early months of the war in 2022, and massively ramped up these attacks at the beginning of last year’s winter, leaving millions of Ukrainians freezing in the darkness of their homes.
A new report published by the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine on Monday and shared with CNN, said these attacks “were carried out with intent” and were in line with Russia’s “state policy to deprive the civilian population from essential energy supplies and cause suffering.”
“Russian commanders who were ordering these attacks knew that the heating facilities they targeted were indispensable to the civilian population, in particular during the winter,” the report, which is being submitted to the UN General Assembly, said.
CNN has approached the Kremlin for comment.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the report “confirms what Ukrainians have experienced for years: Russia’s systematic attacks on civilian energy infrastructure constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity.”
In a post on X, Sybiha said Russia “has deliberately deprived millions of people of electricity, heating and water, turning cold and darkness into instruments of war.”
In a statement released on Monday, the Russian Permanent Mission – the official delegation that represents Russia to the UN – rejected the commission’s findings, claiming it had drawn on “falsified” data and alleging it was set up by a “politicized body.”
“Russia does not recognize the mandate of this commission, which was established through a resolution passed by a politicized body – the UN Human Rights Council,” the delegation said.
“The commission bases its findings on falsified data provided by the Ukrainian authorities via the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) presence in Kyiv,” it added.
The Russian Permanent Mission claimed the UN Human Rights Council “simply fails to notice any crimes committed by the Armed Forces of Ukraine.”
Large-scale Russian drone and missile attacks last winter reduced Ukraine’s thermal power generation capacities by 70 per cent in the most affected areas, according to Kyiv. The suffering was made worse by an unusually cold winter with temperatures dropping to as low as -30 degrees Celsius (-22 F) on multiple occasions.
The commission was established by the UN’s Human Rights Council just days after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
It has previously reported on other aspects of Russia’s war on Ukraine, including allegations of sexual and gender-based violence committed by Russian armed forces, and the wide-spread forced deportations of Ukrainian children by Russian authorities.
Nothing personal between me and Trump, Zelensky tells CNN
In this latest report, the commission describes the dire impacts of prolonged cold exposure on Ukrainian civilians, saying that the country’s medical authorities documented deaths caused by low temperatures in homes, and even in hospitals.
“Medical personnel from hospitals reported that during the past winter, they attended to patients who developed cold-related trauma, including various degrees of frostbite and hypothermia. The patients had developed these conditions at home, due to exposure to unheated premises and required hospitalization,” the report said.
The report quotes a civilian woman living in Dnipro, Ukraine’s fourth largest city, who describes the impact the Russian attacks had on her. “Cold—it paralyzes you; there’s simply no way to get warm, and terrifying thoughts come into your mind,” she said.
The UN commission report names several high-profile Russian officials as the people most responsible for what it describes as “war crimes and the crimes against humanity.”
It says Russian President Vladimir Putin made several “statements concerning instructions to commit attacks against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.”
It also alleges that evidence collected over the past few years shows that Russia’s former Minister of Defence Sergei Shoigu and his successor Andrey Belousov, as well the Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov, have been responsible for planning and overseeing attacks.
The International Criminal Court has previously issued arrest warrants against Putin , Shoigu and Gerasimov for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.
Masha’s husband was fighting on the front line. But she was the one killed by a Russian drone
As the colder weather begins to arrive in Ukraine, Russia has made it clear it intends to continue to terrorize its neighbor.
On Monday night, Russian ballistic missiles hit the grounds of a university in Kyiv, and surrounding areas including near a metro station and residential buildings, Zelensky said in his nightly address. Rescue operations are underway amid reports of people trapped under the rubble, he added.
“The missiles hit very crowded areas, and there is not a single military facility nearby,” the Ukrainian president said. “This was a strike directly on the city, on its infrastructure.”
The report mentions a declaration made by the Russian Ministry of Defence in August, which announced attacks against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and said: “In winter you will freeze.”
Ukraine is increasingly struggling to defend itself against these large-scale attacks because of a critical shortage of air defense missiles. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has made repeated pleas with Kyiv’s western allies for more ammunition, specifically pointing to the upcoming winter as a major worry.
Kyiv had been targeting Russian oil and gas infrastructure, in efforts to hurt the Kremlin’s revenues from energy exports. However, it has eased these attacks after criticism from US President Donald Trump, who has blamed Ukraine for rising gas prices.
The report released on Monday also investigated Russia’s methods of recruiting foreign nationals to serve in its armed forces, concluding they amount to human rights violations and trafficking.
CNN has reported extensively on Russia’s use of deception, bribery and blackmail to lure foreigners into joining its military. People from multiple countries in Africa, India and Latin America have described being promised jobs in Russia only to find themselves on the frontlines.
The commission said it found “compelling evidence” that Russian authorities, working with agents, have “trafficked persons from 29 countries, using deception or coercion, to recruit them in the Russian armed forces.”
It said the fact that Russia has used the same tactics to recruit people from multiple countries “demonstrates a high degree of coordination between agents operating around the world and the Russian authorities.“
“Promised payments and bonuses were usually diverted by recruiting agents and military commanders, passports and phones were often confiscated, and contacts between agents and families were interrupted, once the recruits were deployed to the front.”
The report concludes that Russia violated the recruits’ fundamental human rights, including the rights to life, freedom, health, and to be treated humanely.
The commission also investigated Ukraine’s recruitment of foreign nationals into its army and said that testimonies it collected showed that those joining the Ukrainian armed forces “did so knowingly and voluntarily,” understood the contracts they were signing and received salaries.

articles.title_orig: A 'never-ending' cruise has halted operations and told residents to disembark in Cambodia after fuel costs rose over 300%
articles.title_zh: A 'never-ending' cruise has halted operations and told residents to disembark in Cambodia after fuel costs rose over 300%
articles.content_orig:
A cruise ship selling the promise of a permanent life at sea has come to an abrupt stop.
Villa Vie Residences, which operates the residential cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey , announced on Tuesday that it had suspended operations in Cambodia amid steep increases in fuel costs.
The company said its monthly fuel expenses per cabin, which had previously averaged about $1,800, had risen as much as 344% in parts of Asia, to an estimated $6,000 to $8,000.
The US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, and Iran's subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz — a vital chokepoint for global oil shipments — sent energy prices soaring around the world.
"Since the conflict began in late February, we have taken significant steps to reduce fuel consumption, including slowing the itinerary and spending more time in port," Villa Vie Residences said.
"Those measures have not been enough to offset the extraordinary increase in fuel costs, and we have been unable to continue carrying the resulting operating losses."
Villa Vie Residences sold permanent cabins on its 509-cabin ship, the Odyssey, ranging from $119,999 to $439,999. Its pitch to residents was a never-ending cruise around the world with stops at more than 400 ports of call and a global circumnavigation every three-and-a-half years.
The ship, which has a pool deck, spa, and a pickleball court, also offered five-year residencies, starting at $59,999.
The rising fuel costs put the company's operating model under unsustainable financial pressure, Villa Vie Residences said. The company added that it was evaluating options, but that no financing or transaction had been finalized.

"Passing the full increase on to residents is not a realistic solution," the company said. "Our focus now is on supporting residents, crew, and employees while we work toward restructuring and recapitalization over the next 60 days. That work is ongoing, and no outcome is assured."
The press release said the company was working with residents to coordinate disembarkation in Cambodia and to identify temporary living arrangements for them.
The Odyssey first set sail from Belfast in September 2024 after four months of delays.
Villa Vie Residences did not say how many residents were affected and did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Business Insider.

articles.title_orig: Boeing share price plummets with slower 737 production and free cash flow growth outlook
articles.title_zh: Boeing share price plummets with slower 737 production and free cash flow growth outlook
articles.content_orig:
Boeing doesn't expect to significantly ramp up output of its best-selling 737 Max aircraft until the second half of 2027 as it grapples with a slower-than-expected pace of wing production.
CEO Kelly Ortberg said Tuesday on the company's quarterly earnings call that Boeing is targeting a production rate of 52 planes a month in the second half of 2027. It has been manufacturing about 47 of its 737 Max planes a month.
Ortberg had told investors last month that the production stabilize was taking a "little bit longer" than expected becuase of the wings production pace.
Boeing stock was down about 9% during the call.
"I know everybody wants us to go faster but we're going to do it right," Ortberg told CNBC's Phil LeBeau in an interview Tuesday.
Ortberg reiterated the company's priority in stabilizing production on Tuesday.
"Looking ahead, expectations are rising, and they should," Ortberg said in a note to staff on Tuesday. "That means elevating our performance through lean, productivity and efficiency improvements in our day-to-day work while upholding our high levels of safety and quality."
Aircraft production and deliveries are key to Boeing's recovery since the bulk of an aircraft's price is paid when the customer receives it.
The company also reported Tuesday that it narrowed its losses in the third quarter, thanks to a boost from its defense unit.
For the three months ended Sept. 30, Boeing reported a net loss of $116 million, or 26 cents a share, compared with a $5.34 billion loss, or $7.14 per share, a year earlier. Adjusting for one-time items, the company posted a loss of 34 cents a share. A year earlier, Boeing had taken a nearly $5 billion charge on its long-delayed 777X aircraft program.
Revenue climbed 4% on the year to $24.19 billion. Free cash flow rose to $464 million from $238 million in the third quarter of 2025.
The company's defense unit revenue jumped 15% in the third quarter from a year earlier to $7.94 billion.
Here's what Boeing reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street analysts expected, according to consensus estimates from LSEG:
Boeing delivered 161 commercial airplanes in the third quarter, one more jet than a year earlier.
Revenue in the all-important commercial aircraft business fell 3% to $10.72 billion. The unit had a negative operating margin of 6.5% because of a "less favorable delivery mix, higher projected costs associated with future production rate adjustments and higher estimated supply chain costs," Boeing said.
Ortberg told staff in a memo that the manufacturer has "more work to do."
The manufacturer had some wins lately. The U.S. Navy tapped Boeing to develop its next-generation fighter jet.
And the Federal Aviation Administration last week signed off on the 737 Max 10 , the largest in the Max family. That followed the approval of the 737 Max 7 in August and marked the final certifications for the aircraft line.

articles.title_zh: Exclusive: Meta director Rohit Patel departs after 8 years to take on Microsoft Office Suite
articles.content_orig:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.

After eight years developing AI for Meta, Rohit Patel is departing the company, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. The former director at Meta Superintelligence Labs has launched Ndoc , a startup he’s pitching as an AI-native replacement for Microsoft Office suite or Google Workspace.
Patel is the latest in a handful of high-profile departures from Meta following the exits of Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan , AI researcher Andrew Tulloch , and Head of Product for AI-for-Work Emily Dalton Smith .
Patel designed Ndoc to be more than just another AI tool layered onto an existing workflow. The goal is to replace the fragmented way people work across tools like Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Tableau, Replit, and “ChatGPT copy-paste” with one unified workspace that all colleagues can access, even if they’re not signed up for Ndoc.
Ndoc brings three components together in one layout. The Stage tab is where presentations of key findings live, like slide decks, dashboards, simulations, or mini apps. The Narrative tab features analyses, numbered citations, generated figures, and generally the “why” behind the numbers. The Model tab is where underlying datasets and Python scripts are housed.
The design reflects Patel’s background. During his tenure at Meta, Patel focused on reinforcement learning — a type of machine learning in which AI agents learn to make decisions through trial and error and maximize rewards — and evaluating whether AI output is trustworthy. Patel believes that if AI is going to build the spreadsheets and slide decks that companies use to make decisions, someone should be able to check its work. For instance, users can find the Python scripts used to create the documents.
“Even if you don’t know any Python, you can ask [the AI chat] to explain, ‘Hey, what does this script do? Which line has my formula?’ And you can verify that formula,” Patel said. “There’s nothing hidden behind the curtain here.”
In practice, users can upload a dataset and ask Ndoc to perform an analysis and write a narrative about the findings. They can also add document-specific context, including audience, tone, and memory. “It maintains a memory across your person, that particular document, your team, and your company,” Patel said.
Patel also says Ndoc is built and fine-tuned using a mixture of open source models. Because the platform was developed from scratch, he says it costs considerably less to run than alternatives built on frontier AI models.
“I thought that’s what people would be excited about, but people don’t care about that,” he said, referring to his early trial users. “What people are excited about is that they love seeing all their end-to-end in one place.”
Patel’s larger ambition is to reinvent the file itself. He says documents can be exported as a single “.ndoc.html” file that can be opened in any browser, a format he plans to open-source so other developers can build apps that work with it without being locked into Ndoc the way so many have been locked into Microsoft or Google for years.
His desire to open-source this project was partly why he left Meta and decided to go it alone. At a big company like Meta, getting everyone to agree on an open source format would undoubtedly require the input of “hundreds of people and opinions on how the format should look.”
Patel wanted to move quickly. “Humans can only move at human pace, whereas…I can move at the pace of what AI can do.”
Trying to become the platform where enterprise work happens is a huge bet for a founder with a team of three and no funding, especially when other AI labs are trying to own the same space.
OpenAI, Anthropic , Meta , SpaceXAI , and Google have all come out with enterprise AI tools that allow users to connect to Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and other workplace apps so their AI models can work directly in those tools. And last month, OpenAI launched Space, a shared workspace inside ChatGPT that’s a more direct competitor to those established tools.
Patel acknowledges that Space could be a threat, but says the labs largely have the wrong idea.
“Companies are basically attaching AI to spreadsheets and it fills your cells for you,” he said. “It just sort of kills my soul. This is like if you just figured out electricity, and then you decided the best use case is to put lights on my bulls that till my soil. No. Get a tractor.”
There’s a reason the AI labs have tried to bring their models to where people are already working, though. It’s hard to change habits and replace entire workflows. Patel says he understands that, which is why he built connectors so customers can import existing data from the tools they already use.
“My bar was that I’m not going to release anything I don’t love using,” he said. “I have very optimized AI workflows for everything I do. If I start using this tool, and I keep going back to my workflows, I haven’t built a good enough tool…I have a graveyard of tools that did not meet that bar.”
Patel has a similar bar for gaining customer traction before he tries to raise funds. “I didn’t want to take money until I had some proof that people love the product,” he said.
As of Tuesday, Ndoc is conducting an enterprise pilot and opening an alpha version to a limited number of customers who join the wait list. It’s free to sign up, but customers will pay for usage and tokens. He hopes to release a beta version in the coming weeks, with a full launch planned for next year.
For Patel, moving as fast as possible is more important than having the perfect product from the get-go.
“Execution is extremely cheap…so go execute on a suboptimal plan and worry about it later,” he said. “By the time you make the best plan, the execution will be done by somebody else.”

articles.title_zh: US consumer confidence recovers in October as gas prices eased a bit
articles.content_orig:
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) - Gold prices are trading at session highs after the latest data showed an improving picture of the attitudes of U.S. consumers this month.
The Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.7 in October, above economists’ consensus forecast for an 81 reading and also above the upwardly revised 84.2 print from September, the Conference Board announced on Tuesday.
The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—increased by 8.6 points to 120.4. The Expectations Index—based on consumers' short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions—recovered by 6.9 points to 72.6, only partially reversing three consecutive monthly declines. The survey period for this month's preliminary results was October 1 - 21.
Gold prices were setting fresh session highs in the wake of the 10 am ET data release, with spot gold last trading at $4,048.48 per ounce at the time of writing for a gain of 0.78% on the daily chart.
“Consumer confidence advanced in October, driven primarily by improved perceptions of current and expected business conditions,” said Fergus McCormick, Senior Economist, Global Indicators at The Conference Board. “The recovery was in line with retail gasoline prices easing from September to October. Yet, despite the increase in October, consumer confidence remained on the long-term downward trend that's persisted over the past few years. Consumers planned less spending on services and durable goods over the next six months. This likely reflected higher price levels and persistent inflation, which eroded consumers' purchasing power.”
“Among write-in responses in October, consumers continued to express frustration with rising costs,” he added. “References to prices, the high cost of food and groceries, and oil and diesel prices rose. Comments about war and conflict eased for a second straight month but remained elevated. Mentions of jobs and employment as an area of concern also ticked up, though to a lesser extent.”
“On a six-month moving average basis, only consumers under age 35 and those with a household income of $100k or more expressed an increase in confidence,” the report noted. “By generation, confidence amongst Gen X, Baby Boomers, and the Silent Generation continued to trail significantly behind Gen Z and Millennials, widening a sharp generational divide that has emerged over the past two years. In October, confidence improved across all political affiliations—but much more so for Republicans.”
Consumers' average 12-month inflation expectations declined in October but remained elevated at 5.8%,” the Conference Board said. “Consumers still expected higher interest rates over the next 12 months. Overall, more consumers in October expected stock prices to increase rather than decrease in the next 12 months.”
Jeffrey Roach, Chief Economist at LPL Financial, noted that business conditions and discretionary spending both improved in October.
"Business conditions are the best since April when consensus believed the war with Iran would be short-lived, inflation was less sticky, and the AI-trade dominated headlines," he said. "Even more noteworthy, the top five spending plans included restaurants and movies. Several discretionary sectors are vibrant, although consumers said they will cut back on hotels and airfare."
Roach pointed out that employment opportunities also appeared more plentiful, and home buying plans improved for the third consecutive month.
"Consumers may be tightening their belts, but some experiences are still a priority," he said. "Given the other data on core capital shipments, auto sales, and broader consumer spending, Q3 economic growth will likely be above 3% as the economy plows ahead, elevating annual growth to 2.2% for the full year."

articles.title_orig: AI makes discoveries in mathematics, computer science, physics, OpenAI says
articles.title_zh: AI makes discoveries in mathematics, computer science, physics, OpenAI says
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI has announced that its AI models have made several scientific discoveries in mathematics, computer science and physics.
The AI giant said on Monday that the three new discoveries concerned the fields of harmonic analysis, complexity theory and quantum field theory.
Among the discoveries, AI models proved the local smoothing conjecture, one of the central propositions of harmonic analysis, in every spatial dimension for the first time, according to OpenAI.
Researchers in harmonic analysis, a branch of mathematics that studies how complex signals and functions can be broken down into elementary waves, had previously only proved the theory in three dimensions.
Alex Iosevich, a professor of mathematics at the University of Rochester who specialises in harmonic analysis, said OpenAI appeared to have “cracked” the conjecture in a “historic development”.
“The conjecture was formulated by my PhD adviser, Chris Sogge, so it is near and dear to my heart, and the news was a shock at first,” Iosevich told Al Jazeera.
“Now I am filled with joy and optimism, because the scientific enterprise as a whole is going to make giant leaps as a result of the AI revolution, and we have the chance to be a part of this historic development.”
Iosevich said he expected the field of theoretical mathematics to “change drastically” due to AI.
“I feel a twinge of sadness as a result,” Iosevich said.
“Many theoretical mathematicians I know feel the same way, but I firmly believe that these feelings will soon give way to the realisation that there is so much we can now accomplish.”
“Problems in pure mathematics did not arise in a vacuum,” he added. “Many of them came out of concrete physical considerations, and these connections can now be explored rapidly and decisively.”
According to OpenAI’s announcement, its models also disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, which relates to the time it takes to solve complex computational problems, and provided “mathematically rigorous” proof of quantum chromodynamics, which studies the interaction of quarks and gluons.
Ryan Williams, an expert in computational complexity theory at MIT, said a confirmed refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis would be a major development.
“The ETH has been widely believed true since the late 1990s and a great deal of theoretical computer science was built on it being true,” Williams told Al Jazeera.
“We are working to verify and examine their proof and determine if it holds up,” Williams said.
“Their proof proposes a mysterious new method to more efficiently solve a variety of fundamental problems that have a wide range of potential applications.”
Williams said that while the development would not have real-world applications in the short-term, it could potentially lead to many “future real-world benefits for society”.
“It is hard to predict what will be possible next, because it’s a shocking development,” he said.
The ChatGPT creator said it had reached out to scientists outside the company to turn its “raw research data into scientific understanding”.
The San Francisco-based company said it decided on several different methods for releasing the findings based on consultations with three expert groups chosen to act as “shepherds”.
While the groups collaborating on the mathematics and computer science problems opted to make the AI-produced data public immediately, the physics group decided to defer the release in order to write up their own interpretation of the findings, OpenAI said.
“All of these approaches involve tradeoffs,” OpenAI said.
“On the one hand, the collaborations empower experts to foster unpacking the results and contextualizing them in the broader academic community,” the $852bn start-up said.
“On the other hand, choosing initial shepherds necessarily shapes who gets involved first and creates asymmetry of information. We welcome feedback on how to broaden participation and make this process more useful.”
OpenAI’s announcement is the latest in a series of claimed scientific breakthroughs credited to AI.
Last month, Claude creator Anthropic announced the discovery of a new enzyme said to resemble CRISPR , the groundbreaking gene editing mechanism used in treating conditions such as cancer and sickle cell disease.
Anthropic’s announcement drew mixed reactions among scientists.
While some researchers hailed the finding as an exciting development, others suggested that the AI company had exaggerated its significance.

articles.content_orig:

Ford announced two new EV chargers today that will allow its forthcoming Fathom pickup truck to serve as a battery capable of delivering power to the home or grid.
The new chargers promise to be about half the cost of Ford’s existing equivalent products , which could make the technology available to more households. Ford said the Fathom itself will start at $28,350.
The Fathom will be capable of delivering “over 10 kW” to a home, Ford said. That would allow the electric vehicle to substitute for a small standby generator. For most U.S. homes, it wouldn’t be enough to power everything, but it could keep a refrigerator and air conditioner operational for about half a day.
Such capability has been touted as an advantage EVs have over fossil fuel vehicles, but not many EVs come properly equipped, and the chargers required to make use of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) services tend to be costly.
Ford’s two devices offer similar but differing capabilities.
The Home Power Station device can help customers shave their utility bill by charging the Fathom when power prices are low and sending electricity back to the home when prices are high. The automaker says it will cost around $650, about 50% less than its first-generation bidirectional charger.
The other option, Home Backup Power, is a package that bundles the Home Power Station with a second device, the Home Backup Panel, to allow the Fathom to also power parts or all of a home when the power goes out. Ford says the package will cost around $2,100, about 60% less than its first-generation product.
None of those prices include installation, which for existing V2X chargers can run up to $10,000, depending on how much electrical work needs to be done to prepare the home. Ford did not announce any partnerships with installers, though a spokesperson told TechCrunch that Ford would release more details at a later date.
Which loads the Fathom can power will vary by household and the specifics of each installation. Things like air conditioners and refrigerators, for example, typically require a large surge of power to start up, after which point their load drops. So-called soft-start devices can help mitigate the surge, though they add cost to the installation.
Both chargers will allow Fathom customers to participate in virtual power plants (VPPs), which use software to control a fleet of distributed energy storage devices, such as EVs.
As strain on the grid grows due to AI data centers, utilities have been exploring whether VPPs can help alleviate congestion at the edges.
Fathom owners who enroll and keep their truck plugged in can sell electricity back to the grid, often at a premium. Ford did not say how much Fathom owners can stand to make, but the payouts can be upwards of $1,000 per year, depending on the grid’s needs and the level of participation.
Automakers, including Ford , have been diving deep into energy storage as demand for such services surges. The Fathom-powered VPP is Ford’s latest foray into the market, but it’s unlikely to be its last.

articles.title_orig: UPS Earnings Deliver Good News for the U.S. Economy
articles.title_zh: UPS Earnings Deliver Good News for the U.S. Economy
articles.content_orig:
United Parcel Service on Tuesday reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The guidance raise comes after the company already upped its outlook last quarter . UPS now said it's projecting full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion.
Shares of UPS rose slightly in morning trading.
Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Sept. 30, UPS reported net income of $1.16 billion, or $1.37 per share, down slightly from net income of $1.31 billion, or $1.55, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time expenses, UPS reported earnings per share of $1.69. Revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion.
In its domestic segment, the company said it saw a 4.5% increase in revenue, while its international segment had a 7.1% rise in revenue. Its supply chain solutions business saw an 18.2% revenue increase, which UPS said was primarily driven to growth in forwarding and logistics, including healthcare . On a call with analysts, CEO Carol Tomé said healthcare revenue exceeded $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter.
The company had previously said it expected its third-quarter domestic revenue to be flat and for domestic average daily volume to fall due to seasonal declines and the glide down with Amazon .
"We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network," Tomé said on the call. "All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."
UPS has been in the midst of a turnaround under Tomé's leadership, working to create a leaner business model and leveraging automation to position the company for growth.
As the company prepares for its peak holiday season, Tomé said the consumer remains resilient, and the growth in average daily volume between the third and fourth quarters will be consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume is expected to fall due to the reduction with Amazon.
She added that nearly 70% of all packages will flow through an automated process this holiday season.

articles.title_orig: Argentina Denies Flávio Bolsonaro Entered the Country
articles.title_zh: Argentina Denies Flávio Bolsonaro Entered the Country
articles.content_orig:
Far-right senator on plane to US after missing deadline to hand over his passport since loss to Lula
The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly fled Brazil and is on his way to the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election to the leftwing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
A report by the news website Metrópoles , citing people close to the politician’s family, said he was en route to the US. “The plane is in flight,” Metrópoles reported, without making clear where it had departed from.
Bolsonaro allies told Metrópoles that he would land in Florida on Tuesday afternoon and planned to request political asylum. “The Donald Trump administration has been informed,” the website added.
Allies also confirmed to the Folha de S Paulo newspaper that he was on his way to the US, and said the escape plan had been “organized and enabled by a lawyer close to the Bolsonaro clan”.
“They say the flight should land in a few hours,” the newspaper added.
The news network CNN Brasil reported that Bolsonaro had fled to the US with his wife and two daughters in the early hours of this morning.
Bolsonaro had not been seen since Monday and missed a Tuesday-morning deadline to hand his passport to the federal police, fuelling rumours that he may have fled Brazil after losing on Sunday.
A report in the Brazilian newspaper O Globo said that during a meeting with friends and lawyers on Monday, the defeated candidate had appeared “possessed and made it clear he was afraid of being arrested”.
A supreme court justice cancelled Bolsonaro’s passport minutes after the result in a ruling related to a criminal case against the senator. He had until 11am to surrender the document to the federal police, but did not appear.
The Argentinian news website Infobae reported that on Monday night he reportedly fled to Argentina, where he was expected to board a private jet in Puerto Iguazú bound for the US, but the plane did not take off.
Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede defeat to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, posted a video on Monday in which, commenting on the cancellation of his passport, he said: “I never thought about leaving the country.”
One of the senator’s brothers, the former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, who is in self-imposed exile in the US, had said in an interview last Friday that his brother should leave Brazil if he lost.
The Brazilian newspaper Folha de S Paulo reported that allies in the Bolsonaro family’s inner circle had been told that he had indeed left for Argentina and intended to travel from there to the US.
As there is no record of him passing through any regular Brazilian immigration checkpoint, the federal police are trying to establish from Argentinian authorities whether there is any record of him entering the country.
The Argentinian channel Todo Noticias reported that the senator had reportedly crossed the border into Argentina on foot and abandoned plans to board the plane once news of his movements leaked.
Bolsonaro was told to surrender his passport over a criminal case in which the federal police are investigating him for possible involvement in a money-laundering scheme worth about £680m ($905m) involving betting companies.
The senator’s possible flight makes the future of the far right after the presidential election even more uncertain. The family patriarch, Jair Bolsonaro, is under house arrest for attempting a coup, and one of his sons is in the US and the whereabouts of another unclear.
Eduardo Bolsonaro has an outstanding arrest warrant against him in Brazil, after being sentenced to four years in prison for trying to interfere in his father’s trial by lobbying Donald Trump to impose sanctions on the justices hearing the case.
after newsletter promotion
Political scientist Magna Inácio, a professor at the Federal University of Minas Gerais, believes a power vacuum may now emerge within the right.
“The resistance of Brazilian voters to handing victory to this more extremist camp sends a signal that the right leadership is now up for grabs,” she said.
Since Jair Bolsonaro, then a career congressman with few laws to his name, surprisingly won the presidency in 2018, there has effectively been no right wing in Brazil, only the far-right Bolsonarismo movement.
Camila Rocha, a political scientist who studies Brazil’s new right, believes the fact that three Bolsonaros are now potentially out of the picture could trigger a “shift in power” away from blood ties.
“I think there is a tendency for power to move away from the sons,” said Rocha, noting that before the election, polls showed Jair Bolsonaro supporters preferred other potential candidates over his eldest son, including Jair Bolsonaro’s wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, who was recently elected senator, and the São Paulo governor, Tarcísio de Freitas.
Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly did not want to run because he thought a presidential campaign would turn his life into “hell”, and believed his re-election to the senate was assured. But with Eduardo, his father’s “plan A”, now living in the US, the senator was chosen to run.
Most observers agree that Flávio lacks his father’s charisma. He had a 24-year political career in which he passed very few laws as a state legislator and senator, and the only previous time he ran for executive office was for mayor of Rio de Janeiro in 2016, when he fainted during a televised debate and finished fourth.
Even in a family frequently embroiled in legal trouble he stood out, facing longstanding criminal allegations, including suspicions that he embezzled part of his staff’s salaries, as well as more recent accusations.
Even so, 48.21% of Brazilians voted for Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, which many analysts see as both an anti-Lula vote and a vote for whomever Jair Bolsonaro had chosen.
Inácio believes the struggle over the Bolsonaro legacy will also play out among family members who remain in Brazil, including Michelle and Bolsonaro’s other political sons, the senator-elect Carlos Bolsonaro and congressman-elect Jair Renan Bolsonaro, who publicly do not get along with their stepmother.
“Michelle clearly has a political project of her own, but she is likely to face strong resistance from the two stepsons who are in congress. It is only a matter of time before tensions between them grow,” said the political scientist.

articles.title_orig: Citi and American Airlines refresh 2 credit cards with new perks, higher annual fees
articles.title_zh: Citi and American Airlines refresh 2 credit cards with new perks, higher annual fees
articles.content_orig:
Citi and American Airlines are refreshing two of their cobranded credit cards, adding new earning categories, travel protections and statement credits while increasing both cards' annual fees from $99 to $150. Both cards will continue to offer a $0 introductory annual fee for the first 12 months.
The changes affect the Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® (see rates and fees ) and the Citi® / AAdvantage Business™ World Elite Mastercard® (see rates and fees ).
Beginning Jan. 24, 2027, existing cardmembers will gain access to the new benefits.
Here's a closer look at the changes coming to both cards and what they mean for cardmembers.
Both cards are gaining new ways to earn AAdvantage miles , up to $100 in annual inflight statement credits, a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee credit and travel protections .
The Citi / AA Platinum Select is also adding lifestyle perks, while the Citi / AA Business is introducing a flexible bonus category for eligible business expenses and a discount on a business payments subscription.
Here's an overview of the changes on either card:
According to Citi, both prepaid and pay-later reservations qualify for the new 3X earning rate on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings.
Both cards will retain their existing earning categories, including 2 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases. The Platinum Select will continue earning 2 miles per dollar at restaurants and gas stations, while the Business card will continue to earn 2 miles per dollar spent at car rental merchants, gas stations and telecommunications and cable and satellite providers.
Both cards will also retain the following benefits:
The Platinum Select will also retain up to $180 annually in statement credits (up to $30 per eligible trip) for Turo rentals . The Business card will retain its $99 companion certificate for a single round-trip main cabin domestic flight after spending $30,000 in purchases during the card membership year and renewing the card.
Beyond the new benefits, there are a few key changes worth considering before the refresh takes effect.
Beginning Jan. 24, 2027, both cards' annual fees will increase from $99 to $150. The $0 introductory annual fee for the first 12 months will remain. Existing cardmembers will see the increase at their next renewal after Jan. 24.
The new credits and expanded earning categories could help offset the $51 increase, particularly for those who regularly make inflight purchases or use the Global Entry or TSA PreCheck credit .
For Platinum Select cardmembers, the complimentary Walmart+ annual membership (valued at $98) and 50% discount on an annual FOX One subscription (base membership valued at $199.99 per year) could also help offset the higher fee.
John LaCosta, Citi's head of partnership cards and development for U.S. consumer cards, told TPG that customer feedback helped shape the refreshes, particularly the demand for more everyday earning opportunities, statement credits and travel protections. He said those additions make both cards competitive at their new $150 annual fees.
Combined with the cards' existing benefits, these additions could provide ongoing value. However, cardmembers who don't use the new credits or spend much in the expanded bonus categories may find it harder to justify the higher fee.
Related: How to decide if a credit card's annual fee is worth paying
Both cards are replacing their existing 25% discount on eligible inflight purchases with up to $100 in annual statement credits per calendar year. The new credit covers eligible inflight food and beverages, as well as paid Wi-Fi when complimentary Wi-Fi isn't available.
The full credit can be used on one flight or spread across multiple flights, but Admirals Club purchases are excluded.
LaCosta told TPG that customer feedback helped drive the change, with cardmembers preferring a fixed-dollar benefit they could more easily track and use.
The new credit could offer greater savings. For example, spending $100 on eligible inflight purchases would previously have saved cardmembers $25 with the 25% discount, compared with up to $100 under the new credit.
Business cardmembers will be able to earn 2 miles per dollar in one additional category of their choosing: U.S. shipping providers, office supply stores or U.S. advertising services.
Cardmembers can change their selection quarterly, and those who don't choose a category will default to office supplies.
This could be valuable if your business has substantial shipping or advertising expenses, as there is no cap on the number of miles cardmembers can earn in their selected category.
The card is also adding a 25% discount on a Melio subscription plan, which could appeal to business owners who use the platform to manage payments.
Existing business management tools will also remain available.
The refreshes continue a busy year for the Citi / AAdvantage portfolio, following the introduction of the Citi® / AAdvantage® Globe™ Mastercard® (see rates and fees ) last year and a major refresh to the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® in August .
LaCosta told TPG that Citi has seen Platinum Select cardmembers increasingly use their cards for everyday purchases. "It's clearly a travel card first, but they are more and more becoming top-of-wallet cards for our customers," he said.
Scott Long, American Airlines' senior vice president of AAdvantage, echoed that sentiment, emphasizing that the refreshes are designed to keep cardmembers engaged with the loyalty program even when they aren't traveling.
The new streaming, rides and rails earning categories, along with lifestyle perks like Walmart+ and FOX One, reflect that shift.
Beyond earning redeemable miles, Long also highlighted the ability to earn Loyalty Points toward AAdvantage elite status through everyday credit card spending as a key differentiator for the cobranded cards.
While some competing airline credit cards offer exclusive award discounts for cardholders, American isn't introducing a similar benefit with these refreshes. Long told TPG that the airline continues to evaluate additional ways to deliver value to cardmembers.
The refreshed Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select and the Citi / AAdvantage Business will offer more earning opportunities, new travel protections and additional credits beginning Jan. 24, 2027.
However, the annual fees for both cards will increase by $51 after the first year.
For existing cardmembers, whether the changes are worthwhile will depend on how much value they can get from the new benefits. Those who regularly use the credits or expanded bonus categories may find the higher annual fee easier to justify.

articles.title_orig: Stocks' best stretch of a midterm year starts today, a week before Election Day
articles.title_zh: Stocks' best stretch of a midterm year starts today, a week before Election Day
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Wall Street has spent weeks worrying about AI spending, Big Tech's earnings gauntlet, and the Fed. History says the next eight sessions have tended to reward investors anyway.
Since 1950, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) has risen in 18 of 19 midterm years from five sessions before Election Day to three sessions after, with a median gain of nearly 3%, as Bluekurtic Market Insights pointed out on X. This year's window opens at Tuesday's close, a week before the Nov. 3 vote, and runs through Friday, Nov. 6.
Yahoo Finance reran the numbers and found it's the best eight-session stretch of a midterm year, with the late October start dates ranking at the top of the calendar. No stretch starting at any other time of year has risen more than 15 times in 19.
It also looks like a midterm effect, not just a calendar one. In the other three years of the presidential cycle, the same window rose only 12 or 13 times out of 19.
This year's version is packed, with a Fed decision Wednesday, results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ), and the October jobs report. The S&P 500 sits about 2% below its Oct. 6 record.
The party rarely lasts. The index rose in only 9 of 19 midterm years over the seven sessions after the window, the same hit rate as the week before it.
The longer run is kinder. CFRA's Sam Stovall noted to Brooke DiPalma on Yahoo Finance's Market Domination Monday that stocks have never fallen in the 12 months after Oct. 31 of a midterm year, a record of 19 for 19 by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Jim Paulsen, author of the Paulsen Perspectives newsletter, isn't so sure about this time. He points to tighter conditions over the summer, from higher oil prices to higher bond yields. "I suspect that we're going to have disappointment about this good buying season coming up," he also told Yahoo Finance's Brooke DiPalma Monday.
Bottom line: History favors the bulls the next eight sessions.

articles.title_orig: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
articles.title_zh: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
Apple’s Pro and Tell experience week is here, and it’s off to a strong start, with the new iPad Mini unveiled on Monday morning and a new MacBook Pro and iMac on Tuesday. But there’s more to come: We’re also expecting a long-anticipated touchscreen laptop .
Apple’s had a busy few months, launching the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 , Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the AirPods 5 , followed by the iPhone Duo going on sale at the end of last week.
Apple’s refreshed smart home lineup , revealed during its recent Welcome Home event, is up next: the HomePod Mini 2 will launch on Friday; the Apple HomeView and Apple TV 4K on Nov. 13; and availability for the Home Collection products begins in December.
This week will culminate with Apple hosting a special event on Wednesday, and CNET will be on the ground capturing all the latest details. We’ll update this article as more details are revealed.
Announced on Monday, Apple’s new iPad Mini is available to preorder on Wednesday and will go on sale Nov. 6. It starts at $699 for 128GB of storage, $799 for 256GB and $999 for 512GB.
Setting it apart from the last iPad Mini , which came out two years ago, the new tablet has an 8.5-inch OLED screen (versus an LCD), IP67 water and dust resistance, an Apple A20 processor, a repositioned front-facing camera and a through-screen speaker system called Acoustic Display, as well as being thinner and lighter than before.
The latest iMac, announced Tuesday, features Apple’s M6 processor with a CPU and a GPU each having up to 12 cores, two more cores apiece than before, Apple said. A new dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers AI compute that’s up to twice as fast as the previous generation, the company said. The iMac also has a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display.
Preorders for the iMac M6 will begin Wednesday, Oct. 28, with availability to follow on Nov. 6. Pricing starts at $1,499 for an iMac with M6 featuring a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU. It’s available in seven colors: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange and silver.
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro, also announced Tuesday, similarly features the M6 processor with 12-core CPU and GPU and dual 16-core Neural Engine for AI tasks. Apple says the battery life runs up to 24 hours. The laptop features a Liquid Retina XDR display, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a six-speaker sound system.
The MacBook Pro with M6 can be preordered starting Wednesday, Oct. 28, and will be in stores and delivered to customers starting Nov. 6. Pricing starts at $1,999.
Tuesday also brought updates to the Apple Creator Studio software suite. For instance, Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX, a collection of visual effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates and motion graphics tools; the curated Content Hub now includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro; Pixelmator Pro introduces Generate Fill, which lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language; and Keynote, Pages and Numbers introduce new AI features in beta, including assistants that understand document contexts.
The Apple Creator Studio updates will be available in November to subscribers for free.
And as for the iPhone Duo launch last week, check out CNET’s ongoing folding test — you can watch the livestream here and tune in on Tuesday as we continue testing how many times the iPhone Duo can fold without cracking in the CNET lab.

articles.title_orig: What China’s Patriotic Stock Buying Tells Us About Its Economy
articles.title_zh: What China’s Patriotic Stock Buying Tells Us About Its Economy
articles.content_orig:
US military says the restrictions on the electric vehicles at Kadena airbase also apply to delivery drivers and taxis
One of America’s biggest overseas military bases has banned vehicles made by the Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD over security concerns, the US military in Japan said on Tuesday.
The ban, which went into effect this week at Kadena airbase on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa , has fueled speculation that similar measures could be taken at other US military facilities as part of Washington’s crackdown on Chinese technology it suspects of being used to collect sensitive information.
“These vehicles present an unacceptable and unmitigable risk to our personnel and our mission,” Lieut Col Alli Stormer, a spokesperson for the US air force 18th Wing at Kadena, said in a statement.
The restrictions apply to all BYD vehicles, including privately owned cars, taxis and delivery vehicles, reports said, adding that security personnel stationed at the base’s gates had been instructed to block BYD vehicles and instruct drivers to turn around.
Kadena, the biggest US air force base east Asia, would be directly involved in responding to a crisis involving China , Russia or North Korea .
Its inventory includes the powerful Typhon missile system, which is said to be capable of firing Tomahawk missiles as far as 1,600km, putting parts of China and Russia within striking distance. Kadena also hosts fighter planes and aircraft used for mid-air refuelling, surveillance and reconnaissance, according to its website.
The move comes amid concerns of potential information leaks via vehicle-mounted technologies such as cameras, sensors and GPS devices, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency said.
American military officials have not identified a specific threat, but the ban is part of wider measures taken by the US and other western countries to restrict Chinese smart technology in vehicles, mobile phones and other devices they fear could be used to “spy” on their owners.
In June the Pentagon added BYD to a list of 188 Chinese firms it believes have ties to the country’s military, drawing a protest from Beijing. The blacklist also includes the automaker Nio, e-commerce firm Alibaba and internet company Baidu.
The US defence department banned the sale and use of smartphones from Chinese companies Huawei and ZTE at military bases worldwide in 2018, again citing security concerns.
China has imposed similar restrictions on US-made Tesla vehicles. In 2021, it barred them from some government compounds due to security concerns over ⁠cameras installed on the vehicles. Beijing removed that restriction in 2024 after Tesla won an endorsement from the country’s top auto industry association.
BYD, which has not immediately responded publicly to the Kadena ban, overtook Tesla as the world’s biggest seller of battery-electric vehicles in 2025.
It is now expanding overseas, including in the world’s fourth-biggest auto market, Japan , where in July it launched its Racco electric minicar in the hope that the small, cost-efficient vehicle would carve out a place in a market dominated by domestic brands.

articles.title_orig: Nintendo Indie World Showcase set for October 28
articles.title_zh: Nintendo Indie World Showcase set for October 28
articles.content_orig:
Drop what you are doing. Nintendo just announced a new showcase for this week. We won't have to wait long to find out what the company has in store, as the new Indie World Showcase is being held tomorrow, Oct. 28. Unlike some of the bigger Directs we've seen recently, this will be a smaller affair. That doesn't mean you should miss it, however, as there are still plenty of potential surprises in store.
Thanks to Nintendo's official announcement , we know the latest Indie World Showcase will be roughly 15 minutes long. The showcase will be held at 7:00 a.m. PDT. You can watch it on Nintendo's YouTube channel . The company said that it will focus on "new announcements and updates on indie games coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch."
While we've had a number of big Directs this year, the last Indie World Showcase was held back in March. That event had a number of exciting indies for Switch and Switch 2 owners, such as this year's amazing Denshattack! and the shadow drop of roguelite puzzler Blue Prince on Switch 2.
Since this is an indie-focused showcase, announcements will be from Nintendo's third-party partners. That means you shouldn't expect to see the likes of Zelda, Mario, or Samus, unless they appear in a project like Cadence of Hyrule . Instead, get ready to be introduced to several smaller titles coming in the next few months that are still worth your time alongside juggernauts like the Ocarina of Time remake .
While predicting what will be announced at an Indie World Showcase is a little harder than with a Direct, there is one thing we can all hope for. We know Team Cherry is working on an expansion to last year's game, Hollow Knight: Silksong , called Sea of Sorrow . It has been a while since the developer last shared information, but it was initially announced with a 2026 release date. It wouldn't be impossible for Team Cherry to shadow drop it, or at least reveal the expansion's actual release date. That is, of course, unless it is delayed.

articles.title_orig: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers
articles.title_zh: Apple is adding an AI chatbot to Pages, Keynote, and Numbers
articles.content_orig:
The new AI assistant can draft and restructure content in Pages, while organizing data in Numbers.
The new AI assistant can draft and restructure content in Pages, while organizing data in Numbers.
Apple is bringing an AI assistant to its suite of productivity apps , including Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. The assistant, which is built on AI models from Apple and OpenAI, can understand a document’s context to perform tasks like designing, animating, and refining slides in Keynote.
In Pages, Apple says the AI assistant can draft, restructure, and tweak written content. It can also calculate, visualize, and organize data in Numbers, while suggesting chart types and building custom tables.
Keynote, Pages, and Numbers now support the Model Context Protocol on macOS 27 or later, allowing third-party AI agents to plug into the apps. The AI assistant is rolling out in beta to devices compatible with Apple Intelligence. It works on devices running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, or macOS 27 or later.
Several other updates are coming to Apple’s creative apps as well, with Pixelmator Pro introducing a Generate Fill feature that allows you to edit part of an image by describing the changes you want to see. Apple says the tool “automatically matches the lighting, perspective, and texture of the surrounding environment so edits blend in.”
Meanwhile, Logic Pro for Mac and iPad is getting a Liquid Glass redesign, along with an AI assistant that Apple says can “set up a vocal track from a single prompt” and edit existing projects. There’s also a redesigned Browser on Mac that uses on-device AI to automatically analyze, classify, and tag added sounds.
Apple is launching an update to Final Cut Pro, too, which brings templates, graphics, titles, and transitions directly into the app through MotionVFX. Apple is also building the Content Hub directly into Final Cut Pro, featuring a library of stock videos, photos, and backgrounds. The updates to Apple’s Creator’s Studio will be available to existing subscribers for free in November.
